fontsLoaded: Krona One 400, Familjen Grotesk 400, Familjen Grotesk 600 (all loaded, no MISSING). The 400 italic from the card was dropped because nothing uses it.
deviations: Card fixes applied. (1) Section order re-derived: shelf, then Credits (privacy record as the first thing under the shelf), then Pressed by one person (founder), then Versus, Liner notes, and the back-cover discography moved to the END of the page, where a record's back cover is, so price detail is last. The six FAQ items are split into the sections they answer (tracking and accounts under Credits, who-makes-it under the founder block; money, platforms and alternatives go under the discography and Versus). This is a grouping change, not only an order change. Its order of the named blocks, founder then privacy record then comparison then price, shares at most two items in order with the A/C orders as I could infer them from their cards. I could not see the sibling sketches, so the final check across the three needs the orchestrator. The frame shows the shelf, Credits and the founder block; Versus, Liner notes and the discography are below the frame on desktop, and on mobile the full shelf stack fills the second screen. (2) Drench dropped: the wall is plain white #FFFFFF, black dividers and plank, and the only colour on the page is each app's own spine or sleeve. Cloudberry yellow is gone from tabs, labels and masthead. (3) The studio mark is redrawn as clean inline SVG (24 blocks, ring, 8-point star, gem) and used as a black centre-label roundel in the masthead and as the disc in the founder block. Derivatives and the scroll-padding or sticky-bar contract are not visible in a static frame, so the strip that docks at the top after the shelf scrolls away is not drawn. Other changes: the cartouche (white LAGERLAND plus LGL 019 label) is inset top-left on the sleeve because a full-width white strip would merge with the white wall; the price sticker shows only FREE, with the verbatim price.value 'Free — Premium from $1.99/mo' as a text line (a 64px sticker cannot carry it); the Open button inverts to the sleeve's ink on its ground (a black button would vanish on the dark sleeve); spine price dot is drawn in the spine's ink and means free tier or trial (filled) vs one-time price (ring), derived from price.model, with a one-line legend above the shelf; vertical dimensions tightened (spines 38px, dividers 30px, 2px gaps) so 19 records fit the 1368px shelf. On mobile the newest release sits face-out at the top of the stack (CSS order lift in the build) so the badge and price are in the first 844px; the stack below drops it from Games. Studio swatches (ground, ink) are hand-tuned interim values from the icons, all text on them at least 4.5:1. LGL numbers are computed from release.first_release with slug as tie-break (Xiangqiful = 019). I added one honest line under Credits: the site counts visits with cookieless GoatCounter and the credits describe the apps. Founder name Antti Aittamaa and all FAQ answers are the site's own copy. Mobile bar labels (LGL, price model) are 13px labels, not body text. No screenshot is shown because the card's sleeve carries icon, price, badge and QR only.
selfVerdict: Reads unmistakably as a record-shop shelf and as this style: a white wall, 7 black divider cards, 18 colour spines and one face-out sleeve with the official badge, a QR where the barcode sits, a price sticker and an Open button, all in the first 900px; the mobile first viewport has the same sleeve with badge and price, then a stack of colour bars. It is not the template skeleton: no hero split, no card grid, the catalogue is the page, and below it the proof is a credits sheet with each app's spine laid flat as the row header. Two honest weaknesses: the neutral white wall makes the page stark, and with it dropped the label itself has no colour, so identity rests on type (Krona One) and the cartouche; and with 10 of 19 apps dark, the shelf leans dark-navy/black in places (I tuned swatches to spread them). Vertical spine text is slower to scan than a list, which the mobile stack and the end-of-page discography carry.
